unit_mix.source: Unit sizes from RentCafe / Yardi Matrix D.C. averages; mix proportions held constant across cities so only local conditions vary.

efficiency_ratio.source: Net rentable divided by gross. Held constant across cities.

soft_cost_pct.source: Percent of land plus hard cost. Held constant across cities; priority validation item.

construction_loan_rate.source: SOFR roughly 4.8% plus a 275 to 400 basis point bank construction spread. Reported multifamily construction loan average 7.6%, April 2026. Same in every city; construction debt is priced nationally.

developer_spread.source: Required return over exit cap for a merchant build. Typical range 125 to 175 basis points.

parking_cost_per_space.source: Below-grade structured parking per D.C. Policy Center; overridden where a city uses surface or above-grade parking.

land_cost.source: About $205 per land SF at FAR 3.0, 26% below the $278/SF average asking across 24 listed D.C. parcels. Residual land value at the hurdle is negative, so the conclusion does not depend on this input.

hard_cost_psf.source: Rider Levett Bucknall QCR Q1 2026, D.C. residential multifamily $220 to $370 per gross SF.

parking_ratio.source: Parking minimums bind on 96% of D.C. residential lots.

entitlement_months.source: DOB completes first review within 30 days 97% of the time; delay sits in the discretionary zoning layer above it. Appeals add an average of 450 days.

achievable_rent.source: RentCafe / Yardi Matrix citywide average $2,446, down 3.8% year over year, August 2026.

vacancy_credit_loss.source: Yardi Matrix metro occupancy 94.2%; Northmarq regional vacancy 5.2% at year-end 2025; plus concessions and credit loss.

opex_per_unit.source: Excludes property tax. Elevated by utility distribution charges and BEPS compliance.

property_tax_rate.source: D.C. Office of Tax and Revenue, Class 1A, $0.85 per $100 of assessed value.

exit_cap_rate.source: CBRE Cap Rate Survey, D.C. Class A stabilized infill multifamily 4.75% to 5.5%.

iz_set_aside_pct.source: D.C. inclusionary zoning requires 8% to 12.5% of residential floor area in developments of 10 or more units.

iz_rent.source: Approximately 60% MFI. Refine against DHCD 2026 schedule.

land_cost.source: Priority validation item. No clean public comp source for entitled L.A. multifamily land.

hard_cost_psf.source: Rider Levett Bucknall QCR Q1 2026, Los Angeles residential multifamily $270 to $440 per gross SF. Base at midpoint.

parking_ratio.source: Reduced from historic minimums under AB 2097 near transit; many sites still build to market expectation.

entitlement_months.source: Los Angeles Business Council Institute study (Kung and Gabriel, 2024): completed multifamily projects permitted 2010 to 2022 averaged 549 days awaiting entitlement. Berkeley Law data puts the median for 25 to 49 unit projects at 8.6 months; the mean is pulled up by discretionary projects.

construction_months.source: Same LABCI study: average 863 days in construction after permit.

achievable_rent.source: RentCafe / Yardi Matrix Los Angeles citywide average $2,758, August 2026.

vacancy_credit_loss.source: Yardi Matrix: developers added 11,400 units in 2025; asking rents slid 0.3% on a trailing three-month basis. Deliveries expected to fall to 10,000 in 2026.

property_tax_rate.source: Proposition 13 base rate of 1% plus voter-approved local assessments; L.A. County effective rates typically 1.1% to 1.25% on new construction assessed at cost.

exit_cap_rate.source: Class A primary-market multifamily 4.5% to 5.5% nationally; West Coast infill at the tight end. CBRE flags infill multifamily as the most bearish sentiment in H1 2026.

iz_set_aside_pct.source: Transit Oriented Communities and density bonus set-asides vary by tier; 10% at low-income is a common floor.

land_cost.source: Detroit land is inexpensive; the constraint is not the dirt.

hard_cost_psf.source: Detroit is not covered by RLB. Nearest RLB markets are Chicago ($220 to $490) and Minneapolis ($245 to $435); Detroit builds below both. Base set at $200 pending a local contractor figure.

parking_ratio.source: Surface parking, one space per unit.

entitlement_months.source: Detroit approves quickly. The city wants the building; the appraisal does not.

achievable_rent.source: RentCafe / Yardi Matrix Detroit average $1,324 (July 2026); Yardi Matrix metro report $1,335 (January 2026), up 1.8% year over year.

vacancy_credit_loss.source: Yardi Matrix Detroit occupancy 94.7% in December 2025, above the U.S. average.

property_tax_rate.source: Detroit carries among the highest effective property tax rates of any large U.S. city; new construction without abatement is assessed near 2.5% or above. NEZ and other abatements are the standard workaround and are excluded here to show the unabated case.

exit_cap_rate.source: LoopNet listing analysis puts Detroit's average multifamily cap rate at 11.42% across all classes; Class A new construction trades tighter, roughly 6.5% to 7.5%.

iz_set_aside_pct.source: Detroit's inclusionary ordinance applies only to projects receiving public subsidy or city land.

hard_cost_psf.source: Rider Levett Bucknall QCR Q1 2026, San Francisco residential multifamily $420 to $700 per gross SF, the highest in the country. Base at midpoint.

parking_ratio.source: San Francisco has no parking minimums; maximums apply in most districts.

entitlement_months.source: Berkeley Law Getting It Right data (O'Neill): San Francisco median time to entitlement 25.0 months for all multifamily; 26.1 months for 25 to 49 unit projects. Longest of any California jurisdiction studied.

achievable_rent.source: RentCafe / Yardi Matrix San Francisco average $3,964, August 2026. Yardi reports asking rents up 1.9% year over year through December 2025.

vacancy_credit_loss.source: Yardi Matrix San Francisco occupancy 95.8% as of November 2025.

property_tax_rate.source: Proposition 13 base plus local assessments; roughly 1.2% effective on new construction.

exit_cap_rate.source: Class A primary-market range 4.5% to 5.5%; San Francisco at the tight end on recovering fundamentals.

iz_set_aside_pct.source: San Francisco inclusionary requirement was reduced in 2023 to roughly 12% to 15% on-site depending on project size and district.

hard_cost_psf.source: Rider Levett Bucknall QCR Q1 2026, New York residential multifamily $255 to $500 per gross SF. Base at midpoint.

parking_ratio.source: City of Yes eliminated parking minimums in most of the city in 2024.

entitlement_months.source: As-of-right where zoning allows. ULURP rezoning adds roughly seven months of statutory public review plus pre-certification, typically two years or more end to end.

achievable_rent.source: RentCafe / Yardi Matrix: New York City $4,835 citywide, Brooklyn $3,953, Queens $4,005 (July 2026). Outer-borough figure used since the model building is not a Manhattan tower.

vacancy_credit_loss.source: New York rental vacancy is the tightest of any large U.S. city; Yardi reports asking rents up 5.7% year over year, the strongest of its top 30 metros.

opex_per_unit.source: Excludes property tax. Highest operating costs of the six.

property_tax_rate.source: Class 2 effective rate on new rental construction without 485-x abatement, blended. The published nominal rate is far higher but assessment ratios and caps reduce the effective figure.

exit_cap_rate.source: CBRE H1 2026 Cap Rate Survey: New York City stabilized multifamily widened from 4.5% to 5% in H2 2025 to 5% to 5.5% in H1 2026.

iz_set_aside_pct.source: Mandatory Inclusionary Housing applies only where a rezoning is granted. The as-of-right model building carries none.

hard_cost_psf.source: Rider Levett Bucknall QCR Q1 2026, Miami residential multifamily $190 to $290 per gross SF. Base at midpoint.

parking_ratio.source: Above-grade structured parking, one space per unit.

parking_cost_per_space.source: Above-ground garage per D.C. Policy Center cost benchmarks.

entitlement_months.source: Live Local Act preempts much local review for qualifying projects.

construction_months.source: Concrete construction is standard for wind load.

achievable_rent.source: RentCafe / Yardi Matrix Miami average $2,753 to $2,770, July 2026. Yardi metro report: $2,483 metro-wide, down 0.3% trailing three months.

vacancy_credit_loss.source: RentCafe Miami occupancy 93.3%; Florida statewide multifamily vacancy 7% in tight Miami submarkets to 12% in Jacksonville.

opex_per_unit.source: Excludes property tax. Florida property insurance premiums average more than double the national figure and are the defining cost pressure.

property_tax_rate.source: Miami-Dade effective rate on non-homestead new construction roughly 1.8% to 2.1%.

exit_cap_rate.source: Class A primary-market range 4.5% to 5.5%; Miami posted 8.4% annualized returns in Q3 2025, among the strongest nationally.

iz_set_aside_pct.source: No mandatory inclusionary requirement. Live Local Act projects opt in to 40% affordable for tax benefits; the market-rate model building does not.

bench.name: Benchmark
bench.note: The same building with none of the frictions this publication studies. A reference point, not a real place.

achievable_rent.source: Same rent as D.C., to isolate the cost side.
